title: DMs are where scams start
takeaway: If someone messages you first about mint, prizes or support, treat it as a scam and go to the official channel yourself.

cards.title: You won!
cards.body: It is raffle week. A DM arrives from an account with the Pocket Dragons name, picture and a check mark. It says you won a presale spot and must claim it within the hour. Your heart jumps. Before you tap anything, read it once more, slowly.

seg.label: Greeting
seg.why: Friendly words prove nothing either way.

seg.label: Prize in a DM
seg.why: Prize news that arrives in a DM is a scam pattern.

seg.label: Claim link
seg.why: A link from a DM, not from an official channel.

seg.label: Time pressure
seg.why: A rush is there to stop you checking.

cards.title: Why DMs are the danger zone
cards.body: Anyone can copy a project name, a picture and even a check mark badge. Real support teams and mods do not open DMs about mint, prizes or help. So the safe habit is simple: when a DM starts the conversation, you leave it. Open the official channel yourself and check there.
points: Never open a link that came in a DM.

cards.title: Fake tickets and fake verify bots
cards.body: Fake ticket: someone claims they opened a ticket and sends a link. Open tickets yourself, inside the official server. Fake verify bot: a server asks you to verify, then a page says press Windows and R, paste and press Enter. That command installs malware that steals wallets and passwords.
points: Never paste a command a page or stranger gives you.

cards.title: Close the door
cards.body: Stop strangers in shared servers from messaging you. In Discord, open User Settings, then Content & Social, and turn off Direct messages for your servers. On a phone, tap your profile picture, then the gear. You can also change it for one server at a time. Fewer strangers in your DMs means fewer traps.

cards.title: Try it
cards.body: You joined a new server and a bot greets you. Tap every red flag, then tap Done flagging.

seg.label: Outside verify page
seg.why: A verify step that sends you to an outside site.

seg.t: press Windows and R, paste and press Enter.
seg.label: Paste a command
seg.why: Pasting this runs a command that installs malware.

questions.stem: A DM from "Pocket Dragons Support" says your mint failed and offers help. What do you do?
options: Ignore it and open the official server yourself
Reply with your wallet address so they can check
Tap their link, since it shows your mint status
Ask them to prove they are real staff
questions.why: Support that messages you first is a scam pattern. Go to the official channel yourself and open your own ticket there.

questions.stem: Tap every red flag, then Done.

seg.label: Greeting
seg.why: A greeting alone is not the problem.

seg.label: Prize in a DM
seg.why: Prize news in a DM is a scam pattern.

seg.label: Claim link
seg.why: A claim link from a DM, not an official channel.

seg.t: before your spot goes to someone else.
seg.label: Fear of missing out
seg.why: Pressure is there to stop you checking.

questions.why: Prize news, a link and a rush, all in a DM. Check raffle results only in the official Pocket Dragons channels.

questions.stem: Someone says they opened a support ticket for you and sends a link to finish it. What do you do?
options: Ignore it and open your own ticket yourself
Follow the link, tickets often open on websites
Send your address so they can find the ticket
Check the link has the server name, then open
questions.why: Nobody opens a ticket for you and sends a link. Open tickets yourself, only inside the official server.

questions.stem: A new server asks you to verify by pasting a command into your computer. What do you do?
options: Close the page and paste nothing at all
Paste it, many servers check new members this way
Paste it, but only on a work computer
Read the command first, then paste if short
questions.why: Pasting a command lets the page run code on your computer. In 2025 this trick installed malware that stole wallets and passwords.

questions.stem: You get a DM from an account with the Pocket Dragons picture and a check mark. What does that prove?
options: Nothing, pictures and badges are easy to copy
It is the real team, badges are checked
It is a mod, since it has a check mark
Its links are trusted if the name matches
questions.why: Scammers copy names, pictures and badges. Who messaged first matters more than how the account looks.

questions.stem: Tap every red flag, then Done.

seg.label: Team claim
seg.why: Anyone can claim to be on the team.

seg.t: Here is a private early mint link:
seg.label: Secret early access
seg.why: Secret links in DMs are a classic lure.

seg.label: Friendly line
seg.why: Kind words are normal and prove nothing.

questions.why: A team claim plus a secret link in a DM is a classic lure. Real mint links are posted publicly by the official accounts.

questions.stem: You want fewer scam DMs during mint week. What helps most?
options: Turn off Direct messages for servers in settings
Leave every server except the official one
Hide your wallet address from your profile
Block each scam account after it messages you
questions.why: In Discord, User Settings, then Content & Social, lets you turn off DMs from server members, for all servers or one at a time.

questions.stem: A friend forwards a "winner list" link from a DM. Where do you check if you won?
options: Only in the official Pocket Dragons channels
On the link, since your friend sent it
By asking the DM sender for proof
On any site that shows your wallet name
questions.why: A forwarded link is still a DM link. Results you can trust are the ones in the official channels you open yourself.

seg: I asked a question in the help channel.

seg.label: Noticed your question
seg.why: Anyone can read public channels. Not the problem alone.

seg.label: Ticket opened for you
seg.why: You open tickets yourself, inside the server.

seg.label: Ticket link
seg.why: Tickets never send you to an outside site.

questions.why: Nobody opens a ticket for you and sends a link. That is a fake ticket. Use the official server's own ticket button.

questions.stem: A DM says you must claim your raffle prize in 30 minutes or lose it. Why the rush?
options: To stop you from checking first
Prizes often expire within the hour
The team must close the raffle soon
Unclaimed prizes go to the next winner
questions.why: Urgency is the red flag. A real result is still true after you take time to check it in the official channel.
